title: Nothing can be dropped on an inactive technician, and a failed drop goes back
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser · a way to turn the network off · about 20 minutes
  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043). Desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher).
  • Role: Owner/Admin. On a QA branch sign in with the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView". The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders). This user is the dispatcher.
  • Location: one location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location. Every technician and work order below belongs to this location.
  • Technicians (examples): "ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha", "ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo", and a technician for this case only, "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Dan Delta" (the steps call him Dan). A staff member counts as a technician when, in Settings > Staff > the staff member's edit icon > Edit Staff Member, they are Active, Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customers (used by this case only, each with one contact and one asset): "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Inactive Drop Alpha Co", "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Inactive Drop Delta Co". The steps and expected results call them by the end of the name ("Alpha Co", "Delta Co").
  • Work orders (Approved): lead Ana — Alpha Co; lead Dan — Delta Co.
  • Dan is then deactivated (Active off). Dan's column stays because he still leads Delta Co; its count is 1.
  • None of these technicians has a shift on the Schedule for these work orders (check the Schedule page). If a window titled "Clear … scheduled shifts?" still appears during a move, click "Keep shifts".

Setup

  1. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: confirm "ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha", "ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo" exist and count as technicians at this location (edit icon > Edit Staff Member). To add one: New Staff Member with those settings (at least one Department is required) (e.g. first name "ZZAUTOTEST Ana", last name "Alpha") > Save & Close. Add "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Dan Delta" the same way (first name "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Dan", last name "Delta").
  2. Create this case's customers: "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Inactive Drop Alpha Co", "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Inactive Drop Delta Co". For each: top menu Customers > New Customer, Name > Save; on the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact); then the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2) > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  3. Create each work order listed in the Preconditions: Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. Move it to the status named: a new work order starts as Estimate (it opens with the New Line form: pick a ready-made line and Save & Close); for Approved turn on Line Approved on its line; for In Progress click Start on the line's Labor row (stop the clock afterwards with Stop > Clock Out); for Review click the line's Complete button, type a Tech Story (fill any missing detail it asks for, e.g. Mileage) and click Complete Line (the List shows "Ready For Review"); for Complete then click Mark Reviewed, enter the VIN if asked and click Confirm Review; for Declined save the line with Line Approved off and click Decline on it (it must be the work order's only line); for Invoiced complete and review it first, then Finance tab > Create Invoice; for Paid, after invoicing, Finance tab > New Payment for the full amount > Make Payment. Set the lead technician before invoicing. Once the work order is Approved, pick the technician in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page (leave it as Unassigned for an unassigned one). (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.) Write down each work order number as you create it (e.g. S1-801); the steps call each work order by the end of its customer name (e.g. "Alpha Co").
  4. Then deactivate Dan: Settings > Staff > ZZAUTOTEST F3 Dan Delta > Edit Staff Member > turn Active off > save.
  5. Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All tab > List > type "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Inactive Drop" in Search — exactly 2 work orders show, both Approved: Alpha Co led by Ana, Delta Co led by Dan; in Board View Dan's column is marked inactive with count 1. If anything differs, correct that work order (status or Lead Technician) before starting.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders from the top menu and click the All tab.
  2. Type "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Inactive Drop" in Search so only this case's work orders show.
  3. Click Board View in the display switcher (tooltip "Board View").
  4. Find Dan's column (marked as inactive) and write down its count (1).
  5. Drag the Alpha Co card from Ana's column into Dan's column and release.
  6. Turn this computer's network off (Wi-Fi off or cable out). Leave the page open.
  7. Drag the Alpha Co card from Ana's column into Ben's column and release.
  8. Read the alert, then click its dismiss (X) button.
  9. Turn the network back on and refresh the page.
  10. Open Alpha Co and read Lead Technician.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 5: Dan's column does not accept the card. Alpha Co stays in Ana's column, Dan's count stays 1, and no lead-change message appears.
  • Step 7: the move cannot be saved. The card goes back to Ana's column and the alert reads "Failed to update lead technician, please try again."
  • Step 8: the alert stays until you dismiss it.
  • Steps 9 and 10: after the refresh Alpha Co is still in Ana's column with Lead Technician Ana Alpha.
  • If the app shows its own offline message instead of the alert, write it down. Pass on the card going back and the lead staying unchanged, and note that the alert wording could not be checked this way.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10052 (Story 9, Drag to reorder work and technician groups/columns); SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S9-N2, S4-N5, S4-N3, S4-N8, read 8 Oct 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-N2: “Apply S4-N5’s inactive-destination restriction and S4-N3/S4-N8’s failure recovery to drag reassignment.”
  • S4-N5: “Nothing can be dropped onto an inactive technician's column/group (S2-N2, S3-N2).”
  • S4-N3: “If reassignment fails, return the card or row to its original column or group.”
  • S4-N8: “Failed reassignment shows a user-dismissible alert: “Failed to update lead technician, please try again.””

Last checked against build v26.40.8-7a95011 on 10/8/2026.
